author: Alyssa Tolman
title: Cheyenne Safety Action Plan approved, targets high-risk roads and crash reduction - NewsBreak
text:
By Alyssa Tolman ,
8 hours ago
CHEYENNE — The Laramie County Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved a resolution Tuesday acknowledging receipt and acceptance of the Cheyenne Safety Action Plan, a federally funded initiative designed to reduce serious traffic crashes and fatalities throughout the Cheyenne metropolitan area.
The plan was developed through a Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) grant awarded to the Cheyenne Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO). The federal grant funded the entire planning process, said MPO Senior Planner Jennifer Corso.
“I’ve got to tell you, this is an awesome plan,” Corso told commissioners. “It is our Cheyenne Safety Action Plan. … The federal grant paid for the whole thing, and we’re just going to make Cheyenne safer.”
The yearlong effort was led by Colorado-based consulting firm Felsburg Holt & Ullevig (FHU), and involved representatives from the MPO, Laramie County, the city of Cheyenne, the Wyoming Department of Transportation and other stakeholders.
Lyle DeVries, a staff member with FHU, said the plan focuses on identifying and addressing locations where severe crashes, serious injuries and fatalities occur most frequently.
“The focus is really on action here,” DeVries said. “Taking action to reduce severe crashes throughout the Cheyenne MPO area.”
The project included examining five years of crash data across both urban and rural portions of the metropolitan planning area. Researchers analyzed crash trends and paired that information with public feedback gathered through online surveys, community events and stakeholder meetings.
DeVries said community input was a key component of the planning process because some safety concerns may not have been reflected in crash statistics alone.
“There are places where people don’t feel safe, there are persistent safety problems that don’t bear out in the data,” DeVries said. “So it’s important to have conversations with the community, understand where they feel at risk and what they experience as safety concerns, and pair that with the data.”
The analysis resulted in the creation of a high-injury network map identifying roadways and intersections with disproportionate numbers of severe crashes. Corridors highlighted in the plan include Dell Range Boulevard, South Greeley Highway and several other major transportation routes in Cheyenne.
The completed plan outlines dozens of infrastructure projects prioritized over short-, medium- and long-term timelines. Fifteen projects were identified as near-term priorities due to higher crash rates or increased risks to pedestrians, bicyclists and other vulnerable road users.
An additional 16 projects were categorized as mid-term improvements, and 28 were placed in the long-term category.
Beyond specific projects, the plan also includes a toolkit of safety countermeasures and policy recommendations intended to guide future transportation investments and decision-making.
The Cheyenne MPO Policy Committee officially approved the plan last week. DeVries said the next step will be implementation by local agencies, including the county, city and WYDOT.
“In the future, it is the aim of this plan to not remain on the shelf, but be referenced frequently to help inform decisions about safety and transportation funding moving forward,” DeVries said. “There’s also the opportunity to monitor and have accountability for progress moving forward.”
The plan includes a public dashboard that will track severe crashes and allow agencies to monitor progress over time.
Commissioner Troy Thompson said he appreciates the MPO’s work and encouraged residents to review the plan.
“This is fascinating stuff to look at,” Thompson said. “As you’re looking through the packet that’s in our file here, all of the accidents and the severe accidents and where they’re happening, it’s pretty fascinating stuff. So, if people are interested, this should all be on our website if they want to look at it.”
The resolution passed unanimously. A copy of the action plan, and other related documents, can be viewed at plancheyenne.org/safe-streets-4-all/ .
